messages.content: When will be sunset in Beijing today?

function.name: calculate_sunrise
function.description: Calculate the time of sunrise for a specific date and location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location for which sunrise time needs to be calculated.

date.description: The date for which sunrise time needs to be calculated in YYYY-MM-DD format. If not provided, current date is considered. Default: 1998-12-03

format.description: Format in which the time should be returned. If not provided, default format 'HH:MM' is considered.

message.reasoning:
We need to calculate sunset time. The tool only calculates sunrise. We can use sunrise to compute sunset? Not directly. We might approximate sunset as sunrise + daylight duration. But we don't have daylight duration. We could use sunrise function to get sunrise time, then approximate sunset by adding daylight length. But we don't have daylight length. We could approximate using known formula: daylight length depends on latitude and day of year. But we don't have a function for that. We could approximate sunset as sunrise + 12 hours? That would be wrong. We could approximate sunset as sunrise + 12 hours minus some offset. But we don't have data.

We might need to call the function to get sunrise, then manually compute sunset. But we don't have daylight duration. We could approximate daylight duration using known formula: daylight hours = 2 * arccos(-tan(lat)*tan(declination)) / 15. But we don't have declination. We could approximate declination using day of year. But we don't have day of year. We can compute day of year from date. Today is 2026-06-04. Day of year: Jan 31 days, Feb 28 (2026 not leap), Mar 31, Apr 30, May 31, June 4 => 31+28+31+30+31+4 = 155. So day 155. Declination approx: -23.44 * cos(360/365 * (day_of_year + 10)). But we don't have a function. We can approximate. But we might not need to be exact. We can approximate sunset as sunrise + daylight duration. But we don't have sunrise time. We can call function to get sunrise. Then we can approximate daylight duration using formula. But we need to compute declination. We can approximate declination: δ = -23.44 * cos(360/365 * (day_of_year + 10)). Let's compute: day_of_year + 10 = 165. 360/365 ≈ 0.9863. 0.9863 * 165 = 162.7 degrees. cos(162.7°) = cos(180-17.3) = -cos(17.3°) ≈ -0.956. So δ ≈ -23.44 * (-0.956) = 22.4°. So declination ~22.4°.

Latitude of Beijing: 39.9042° N. So we can compute hour angle: cos(H) = -tan(lat)*tan(δ). tan(39.9042°) ≈ 0.823. tan(22.4°) ≈ 0.409. Product = 0.823*0.409 = 0.336. Negative: -0.336. cos(H) = -0.336. So H = arccos(-0.336) ≈ 110.4°. In degrees. Convert to hours: H/15 = 7.36 hours. So daylight duration = 2*H/15 = 14.72 hours. So daylight ~14h43m. So if sunrise is at X, sunset = X + 14h43m.

Now we need sunrise time. Use function calculate_sunrise with location "Beijing" and date "2026-06-04". Format default HH:MM. Let's call function.
